transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, well... I guess my work physical is actually what got me here. The doctor there told me that my weight is, well, he said it's a bit too low. 

But honestly—and I hope it's okay to say this—to me, I just feel a lot lighter on my feet for basketball. And at the garage, I'm a mechanic, I just don't feel as weighed down when I'm working under the cars all day. That's a good thing, right? I mean, I hope that makes sense. I feel pretty good, but I wanted to do what the work doctor asked and come see you, just to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

Um... I don't know if I'd use the word "worried," exactly. I just like staying on top of my game, you know? 

But... well, I guess if I'm being totally honest—and I hope this doesn't sound silly—if I see the scale bump up even just a single pound, or if my work jeans start feeling a little tighter, I do get a bit bothered by it. I just start thinking I'm getting soft, and that I'll end up being slower moving around the cars at the shop, or up and down the court. I just want to stay quick so I can keep doing a good job. That's a pretty normal way for a guy to look at it, isn't it?
Do you think you look too thin or just right?

Um, well... I guess I think I look just right. I mean, maybe a little lean, but that's what I'm aiming for, you know? 

I don't think I look *too* thin. I just look fit. Like I said, it helps me move better at the shop and on the court. When I look in the mirror, I just see a guy who's keeping himself in shape. I don't look sick or anything like that. At least, I don't think I do. Does that sound okay to you? I mean, being lean is generally a good thing for your health, right?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Well, um... "afraid" sounds a little intense, I guess. I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around terrified or anything. But it's, um, it's really just like what I was saying a second ago. 

If I see the scale bump up even a single pound, or if my jeans feel tighter, my mind just goes straight to thinking I'm getting soft. And I really don't want to end up being slower moving around the cars at work, or dragging up and down the basketball court. So maybe not *afraid*, but I definitely try hard to avoid it so I can keep doing my job well. That makes sense, right?
Have you been changing what or how much you eat to maintain your current weight?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say I'm really changing things, exactly. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing anything strange. It's mostly just... being practical, I think? 

Like, most days, I just keep it to coffee in the morning to get going. And then later on, maybe just a small sandwich or, you know, half of whatever's around. It's just that the shop is always running late, and the house is always so busy, so I just... I feel better sticking to my own simple rules. It keeps things easy and keeps me moving without feeling weighed down. A lot of guys eat light when they're busy working on cars all day, right? That's not a bad way to handle it, is it?
Do you think about how the food you eat will affect your body shape or appearance?

Um, well... I mean, a little bit, maybe? But not in a bad way, I don't think. I hope that doesn't sound vain or anything.

It's more just... I like to look neat and put together, you know? Like, if I eat too much junk, I feel like I look sluggish, and I don't want the guys at the shop or the customers thinking I'm letting myself go. So I guess I do think about it a little, just to make sure I still look like a guy who works hard and stays active. That's pretty normal for guys my age, though, isn't it? Just wanting to look decent?
Do you ever think about your weight or body shape when you're not getting ready for work or playing basketball?

Well, um... no, not really, I don't think. I try not to, anyway. Like, if I'm just hanging around the house on a Sunday or catching a game on TV, I'm not really dwelling on it. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting there obsessing over my stomach while I'm on the couch or anything weird like that. 

It's really just tied to making sure I'm fit enough for the shop and the court, like I mentioned. Once I'm off the clock, I just try to relax and not worry about it too much. It's healthy to kind of switch off like that, isn't it?
Has your focus on weight or body shape ever affected your relationships with friends or family?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's a big problem or anything. I mean, I'm still keeping up with everything at the garage just fine, and I haven't missed a beat in my basketball league. So I'm still doing all the normal stuff, I promise. 

But, I guess... well, maybe it has caused a little bit of tension at home lately. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad guy. It's just that I kind of avoid sitting down for the regular family meals. You know how heavy those dinners can get, and I just feel better sticking to my own routine. 

Because I do that, though, people keep asking if I'm okay. Which is nice of them to care, but I hate making anyone worry when I'm just trying to stay fit. It's pretty normal to skip a big, heavy dinner if you're trying to stay active and light for the court, right? I'm not doing anything wrong by just eating on my own schedule, am I?
Do you think you would still try to maintain your current weight if you weren't playing basketball?

Um, well... I mean, I guess I'd probably still want to keep it around where it is? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm too focused on it. 

Even if I wasn't playing, I'd still have the shop to think about, you know? It's a physical job, being on my feet, getting under cars... I just want to make sure I don't get out of shape and start slowing down at work. I don't want to be the guy holding everyone else up because I let myself go. 

So, yeah, I'd probably still try to eat light and stay active, just to be healthy and do my job right. That makes sense, doesn't it? It's just about being responsible and taking care of yourself, right?
Do you think you would be less strict about your eating habits if you didn't have to perform well in basketball?

Um, well... I don't know if I'd really call it being strict, to be honest. I definitely don't want you to think I'm on some kind of extreme diet or anything. Even if I wasn't playing ball, I think I'd probably still eat about the same way. 

It's just... well, most days I keep it to just coffee in the morning, and then maybe a small sandwich or, you know, just half of whatever is around later on. It's not really about punishing myself or being rigid, I promise. It's just that with the shop always running late and things being so busy around the house, I just feel a lot better sticking to my own simple rules. It keeps things predictable, you know? 

That's a pretty normal way for a busy guy to manage his day, isn't it? Just keeping it simple so it doesn't get in the way of work?
Do you think you would eat more if you didn't think it would affect your weight?

Well, um... I guess maybe I would? A little bit? I mean, I don't want you to think I'm obsessed with the scale or anything like that. I really just try to be mindful. 

It's just... if I see the number on the scale bump up even a pound, or if my work jeans start feeling even a little bit tighter, I just... I start worrying that I'm getting soft, you know? Like I'm letting myself go. And if I get heavy, I'll be slower moving around the cars at the shop, or I won't be able to keep up with the younger guys on the court. 

I just want to stay sharp and capable. It's pretty normal to want to avoid gaining weight so you don't lose your edge, right? I'm just trying to stay in good shape for my age, that's all.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you didn't fear gaining weight?

Um, well... I guess if I really wasn't worried about gaining weight at all, things might be a little different. But I don't want to make it sound like it's this huge fear that runs my life, you know? 

It's just that... well, like I was saying before, if I see the scale bump up even a single pound, or if my work jeans feel just the slightest bit tighter around the waist... I just start thinking I'm getting soft. And I really don't want to get soft. If I put on weight, I just know I'll be slower moving around the cars at the shop, or dragging when I'm running up and down the court. 

So I guess, yeah, if I didn't worry about getting slow and soft, maybe I wouldn't be as careful. But it's just about wanting to stay on top of my game, right? That's a pretty reasonable way to look at it, don't you think?
Do you think you would still feel good about your body if you gained a few pounds?

Um, well... I really don't think I'd feel great about it, to be perfectly honest. I mean, I hope that doesn't sound vain or anything. I don't want you to think I'm obsessed with my looks. 

It's just, like I mentioned earlier, if I see the scale bump up even a pound, or if my jeans start feeling tighter, I just... I start feeling like I'm getting soft. And I really hate that feeling. If I gain weight, I know I'll be slower moving around the cars at work, and I won't be able to hustle on the court. 

I just want to feel capable and strong, you know? So gaining a few pounds... I think it would just make me feel like I'm losing my edge. That makes sense, right? It's pretty normal to want to feel good in your own skin and stay active, isn't it?
Do you think your desire to stay lean is more about avoiding weight gain or about performing well in basketball and at work?

Well, um... I guess it's a little bit of both? But I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm just terrified of getting fat. I know that sounds kind of... well, not great. 

But honestly, if I see the scale bump up even a pound, or if my jeans feel tighter, I just... I start thinking I'm getting soft. And I really don't want to get soft. I just know that if I do, I'll be slower moving around the cars at work, or I'll be dragging up and down the court. 

So I guess avoiding the weight gain is how I make sure I can still perform well. They kind of go hand in hand, right? I mean, it's pretty normal to want to stay lean so you don't lose a step, wouldn't you agree?
Would you say your main goal is to avoid gaining weight or to perform well in basketball and at work?

Um, well... I mean, I guess it's hard to separate the two, you know? But I really want to make sure I'm being clear that I'm not just, like, obsessing over the number on the scale for no reason. I hope I'm explaining this right.

It's just... like I've been saying, if I notice the scale go up even a single pound, or if my work jeans are just a tiny bit tighter... my mind just immediately goes to, "I'm getting soft." And I really, really don't want to be soft. Because if I am, I just know I'll be sluggish under the cars at the shop, or I won't be able to keep up on the court. 

So, I guess... avoiding the weight gain is just my way of making sure I can still do the things I need to do. It's just practical, right? That makes sense to you, doesn't it?
Do you think you would still restrict your food intake if you weren't concerned about your athletic performance in basketball?

Um, well... that's a good question. I mean, I guess even if I wasn't playing basketball, I'd probably still keep things pretty simple with my eating. I hope that doesn't sound like I have some kind of eating problem. I just... I like having a routine, you know? 

Most days I just keep it to coffee in the morning, and then maybe a small sandwich or just half of whatever is around later on. It's just easier that way. With the shop always running late and then coming home to a busy house, I just feel better sticking to my own simple rules. It keeps me from feeling weighed down or, you know, soft. 

It's just a practical way to manage a busy schedule, right? I mean, a lot of guys my age probably do the same thing to stay on top of things, wouldn't you say?
Would you say that your eating habits are mainly controlled by your desire to maintain a certain weight?

Well, um... "controlled" makes it sound a little intense, you know? I really hope I'm not coming across like someone who's, like, obsessed with their weight. I just try to be careful. 

But, yeah, I guess like I was saying before... it really just boils down to how I feel physically. If I see that scale bump up even a pound, or if my jeans feel tighter, I just start thinking I'm getting soft. And I just can't afford to get soft, because then I know I'll be slower moving around the cars at the shop, or I'll be dragging up and down the court. 

So I guess maintaining my weight does dictate how I eat, yeah, but mostly just because I need to stay quick on my feet and do my job well. That's a pretty normal way to look at it, right? I mean, you can understand why I'd want to keep it in check?
Do you think you would eat normally if you didn't fear gaining weight would affect your performance at work or in basketball?

Um... wow, that's... I mean, that's kind of hard to picture, honestly. I hope I'm not sounding too difficult here, but... it's just so tied together for me. 

If I didn't worry about the shop or the court... I mean, maybe I'd eat a little differently? But, honestly, even if I wasn't working or playing ball, I think I'd still be really careful. It's just... like I mentioned, if I see the scale bump up even a single pound, or if my work jeans feel even a tiny bit tighter, my brain just immediately flashes to "I'm getting soft." And I just... I really hate that feeling. I don't want to be soft. 

So, I think the fear of that happening—of feeling sluggish or heavy—would still be there, even without the basketball or the cars. I just want to feel sharp, you know? I hope that makes sense... does that sound okay to you?
Would your eating habits change if your job at the garage didn't require you to be physically active?

Um... well, I guess if I wasn't moving around so much at the garage... I mean, I'd like to think I'd eat a little more normally. I hope that's the right answer. But honestly, I'm not entirely sure. 

Even if I was just sitting at a desk all day, I think I'd still be pretty careful. Like I was saying, it's just really important to me not to feel soft or heavy. I think I'd probably still stick to my routine because... well, I'd probably be even more worried about the weight creeping up if I wasn't on my feet all day. 

It's just about staying healthy and disciplined, right? I mean, a lot of guys watch what they eat when they have sedentary jobs, don't they? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Would you say that your fear of gaining weight or your desire to perform well in basketball and at work is more influential in determining what and how much you eat?

Um... that's a tough one to separate, to be honest. I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I think they kind of feed into each other? 

Like, I want to do a good job at work, and I want to keep up with the guys on the court. But... if I'm being completely honest, the fear of gaining weight is probably the bigger driver. It's just... like I said earlier, if I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound, or if my jeans feel even a fraction tighter, my mind just goes straight to, "I'm getting soft." 

And then I start worrying that because I'm soft, I'll be sluggish dodging around the lifts at the shop, or I'll be dragging my feet on the court. So the performance thing is definitely there, but it really starts with that panic about the weight going up. I just really, really don't want to let myself go. That makes sense, doesn't it? I mean, wanting to stay in good shape is a positive thing, right?
